# check-licence-mentions.sh reads every line with one of its words, in any
# case, of every text file under nightjar/ and rubylight-native-api/ but
# nightjar/LICENSE.txt and rubylight-native-api/LICENSE. This file records
# each such line word for word, with its file and what covers it in the
# notices of what ships nightjar-core. Its words:
# - anywhere in the line: "licenc" and "licens", "copyright", "public
#   domain" (also with "-", "_" or nothing between), "©", and "(c)" before a
#   year;
# - with no letter, digit or underscore just before: "GPL", "LGPL", "AGPL";
# - as whole words, also with a version glued on: MIT, BSD, 0BSD, Apache,
#   ISC, Zlib, MPL, CC0, CC-BY, BSL, Boost, EUPL, WTFPL, OFL, EPL, CDDL,
#   Artistic, Unicode-DFS, "Unicode-" and a digit, SSLeay, and "(c)".
#
# The second field is what covers the line:
# - a part title: the notices' part of that name (`nanors`, and `nightjar-core
#   and the Rubylight crates` for the GPL-3.0 code that nightjar-core ports
#   from the projects that part names);
# - `crate:NAME`: cargo-about lists the crate NAME and its licence;
# - `-`: the line names no licence of the code (a crate's name in a lock
#   file, a field that defers to the workspace, a product feature, a word in
#   prose).
#
# Both notices' builds fail on a line with one of the words that is not
# recorded here, a new one in a listed file too; on a recorded line that its
# file no longer has; and on a part or crate that the notices lack. A person
# reads each new line and records it. The script's header lists what it does
# not catch, so read the header of each new source file when the pin moves.
#
# Tab-separated: FILE<TAB>PART<TAB>LINE.
nightjar/protocol/Cargo.lock	-	 "zlib-rs",
nightjar/protocol/Cargo.lock	-	name = "zlib-rs"
nightjar/protocol/Cargo.toml	nightjar-core and the Rubylight crates	license = "GPL-3.0-only"
nightjar/protocol/client/Cargo.toml	-	license.workspace = true
